meta.scope: Publicly disclosed data center leases from public-company press releases, 8-K exhibits, and investor materials. The universe skews toward converted-miner developers because hyperscaler-direct leases with private developers are rarely disclosed.

conventions.mw: criticalItMw is the billable denominator. grossMw is utility/gross power and is shown for context only.
conventions.null: null means undisclosed. The engine treats null as unknown, never as zero.
conventions.basis: Every quantitative field carries a companion basis flag where it matters: stated (from filing or release), derived (computed from other stated values), estimated (Claude/Jae estimate, flagged in UI), unverified (secondary source only).
conventions.dates: YYYY-MM-DD for events, YYYY-Qn for delivery windows

creditTiers.1: Investment-grade hyperscaler, IG parent guarantee, or IG credit support covering the lease
creditTiers.2: Well-funded private AI lab or AI cloud without disclosed IG support

deals.campus: Six-site portfolio (Denton TX, Dalton GA, Muskogee OK, Marble NC, Austin TX)
deals.renewalOptions: Two 5-year options (Austin site is a 7-year term)
deals.rentCommencement: Rolling by site from 2025 through early 2027
deals.tenantFundedCapexNote: Up to $1.5M per MW (about $750M) funded by CoreWeave and credited against hosting payments at no more than 50% of monthly fees until repaid. Core Scientific separately funds $104M for the Denton 70 MW increment with no credit.
deals.capexNote: Tenant-funded model. Developer net spend is undisclosed; the only stated figure is $1.5M per MW for the Denton 70 MW increment. Because total developer capex is unknown, the global capex assumption applies and yield on cost is likely understated for this deal.
notes: Cleanest public example of tenant-funded capex repaid through rent credits. Headline $/kW/month is not comparable to NNN leases without adjusting for the credit.
Company guided to 75% to 80% margin, so revenue is well above NOI; the engine applies the opex assumption slider here unless NOI is entered.

CoreWeave announced an agreement to acquire Core Scientific in May 2026 (a prior 2025 attempt did not close). If completed, the tenant becomes the owner and this lease converts from third-party rent to internal cost.

deals.renewalOptions: Two 5-year options; roughly $7B if exercised (initial 168 MW tranche)

notes: Textbook effective-credit case: nominal tenant is a private AI cloud, but Google backstops about $1.4B of roughly $3B base-term obligations (about 47%). The engine blends the credit score by coverage (0.47 x Tier 1 + 0.53 x Tier 3) and displays the result as Tier 2.
Same developer as the AWS deal, which makes CIFR-AWS vs CIFR-Fluidstack a clean rate-versus-credit comparison on one balance sheet.
